title: Holmes OSF · Supplementary Experiment 5, intensity-ratio follow-up
citation: Holmes, N. P., Martin, D. J., Mitchell, W., Noorani, Z., & Thorne, A. (2020). Do sounds near the hand facilitate tactile reaction times? Four experiments and a meta-analysis provide mixed support and suggest a small effect size. OSF 73x59, manuscript revision 4.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

reference_parameters.planner_scope: The source settings describe this companion procedure. The Planner contains no executable trial schedule for it.

published_method.scope: One highly trained observer completed an additional session after the three-observer feasibility series.
published_method.task: Classify a single vibration as weak or strong. Its weak reference is the observer's 90% threshold. The assigned ratio scales the stronger vibration.
published_method.outcome: Compute proportion correctly categorized per mask and ratio block. Supplementary Fig. 4 depicts chance reference and author-reported above-chance blocks. Trial counts, multiplicity treatment and exact block order remain unresolved.

stimulus_type.value: Single tactile vibration classified under continuous or discrete white noise.
stimulus_type.source: Holmes et al., publisher/OSF Supplementary Materials, printed pp. 24–26, Supplementary Experiment 5 and Supplementary Fig. 4

source_provenance.gap: The original ratio session source code and data are unverified. Physical comparability with Experiments 1–4 is unestablished.
